SETTING (blocks 39 and 40, open PRs titled 'ail39: records that move' and 'ail40'): records move and carry their content; a site is empty or holds one record; two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega (omega the rule's pair weights), a bond with an empty end weighs 1, a record weighs z; motion is pair-weight transit, in detailed balance with this law; formation happens at rate z * Z_x with content drawn from the rule. THE PINNED SCALE: c = c_0, the value at which W is the rule's one-neighbour probability divided by the uniform probability (six axes: c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r), W = 6 K_1; sphere menu with omega = exp(beta s.s'): c_0 = beta/sinh(beta), W = the density of the rule against the uniform measure). At c_0: an empty site acts on each neighbour as a record of unknown content; the law with vacancies is reflection positive through bond planes (and not below c_0); on any window without a cycle the occupancies are independent with density 6z/(1 + 6z); a fully occupied cycle of length n carries the factor 1 + 3 l_1^n + 2 l_2^n with l_1 = (p - q)/(p + q + 4r), l_2 = (p + q - 2r)/(p + q + 4r). The owner has accepted c = c_0 as the working value; it is not registered. At c_0 records interact only through cycles, with factors computed from the rule's eigenvalues l_1, l_2. TASK: (a) the exact expansion of the law of the occupied set on a finite window as a sum over cycle structures (for a unicyclic occupied set the factor is 1 + 3 l_1^n + 2 l_2^n; for two cycles sharing edges compute the factor by the transfer of K_1 and show the general rule); (b) a convergent expansion of the density-density correlation on the cubic lattice at small l_1, l_2 and an explicit region of (p, q, r, z) where the density is analytic in z (no clumping), with exact small-window checks; (c) a contour or chessboard argument (reflection positivity holds at c_0) for a dense aligned phase coexisting with a dilute one at large l_1, with an explicit region; (d) compare with the executed onsets on the line (p,1,2): above 16 at density 0.1, 8-12 at 0.3, 6-8 at 0.5, below 6 at 0.7.
